target: Jag ska åka till Norge imorgon nu.
english: I'm going to go to Norway tomorrow now.
tip: "Ska" + infinitive expresses plans/intentions. The most common future form.

target: Huset hade stått tomt sedan lång tid tillbaka.
english: The house had stood empty for a long time.
tip: The pluperfect is hade plus the supine: hade stått = had stood, an action before another past point.

target: Vi skulle vilja boka ett bord för två.
english: We would like to book a table for two.
tip: "Vi skulle vilja" is the most formal way to make a request.

english: The lake glitters in the sun.
tip: Both "sjön" and "solen" are simple definite – no double definite needed.

english: The food is cooked by the chef.
tip: For habitual or general statements the s-passive wins: maten lagas av kocken adds -s to the verb instead of using bli.

target: Boken har översatts till tjugo språk.
english: The book has been translated into twenty languages.
tip: Perfect passive is har plus the -s supine: boken har översatts = the book has been translated.

target: Platsen dit vi reste på kvällen förra året.
english: The place we traveled to in the evening last year.
tip: Dit means 'to where' and marks motion: platsen dit vi reste. Där means 'where' for a static location.

english: The door opens automatically.
tip: Here "-s" makes it passive: 'the door is opened.' Context tells passive from deponent.

english: The memory that remains.
tip: Kvar means left or remaining. Stannar kvar means stays behind or lingers, adding the sense of not going away.

english: The park that we visit.
tip: When som is the object of the clause you can drop it. Parken vi besöker means the same as Parken som vi besöker.

english: People who talk a lot.
tip: Swedish uses one word, som, for both who and that. Människor som pratar covers people who talk and things that do.

english: The trip was booked online.
tip: Past passive adds -s to the past tense. Bokade plus s gives bokades, meaning was booked, with no helper verb.

english: What makes Sweden unique.
tip: Det som means what, in the sense of the thing that. Det som gör covers what makes or what does something.

english: The music being played is nice.
tip: "Som spelas" = that is being played. S-passive in relative clause – very natural in Swedish.

english: He who asks gets an answer.
tip: Den som means whoever or the one who. Den som frågar = whoever asks, used for general statements.

english: The man whose dog ran away.
tip: Vars means whose, the possessive relative word. Mannen vars hund = the man whose dog. It never changes form.

english: The door was opened by the wind.
tip: Blev plus a participle like öppnad builds a passive for one completed event, unlike the -s passive for general facts.

english: The bridge was built for two years.
tip: Under with a time span means over or during. Under två år = over a period of two years, not underneath anything.

english: The language is spoken by ten million.
tip: In a passive, av marks who does the action. Talas av tio miljoner = spoken by ten million.

target: Något som jag aldrig har sett.
english: Something I have never seen.
tip: Inside a som clause the adverb comes before the verb. Jag aldrig har sett, not jag har aldrig sett as in a main clause.

target: Allt som allt är jag nöjd.
english: All in all I'm satisfied.
tip: Allt som allt is a set phrase meaning all in all or all things considered. It is not read literally.

target: Så vitt jag vet stämmer det.
english: As far as I know, it's correct.
tip: Så vitt jag vet is a fixed phrase for as far as I know. Vitt here is not the color white.

target: Inte förrän klockan tre fick vi svar.
english: Not until three o'clock did we get an answer.
tip: Inte förrän means not until. Starting a sentence with it flips verb and subject, so it is fick vi, not vi fick.

target: Klänningen som hon har på sig är fin.
english: The dress she is wearing is nice.
tip: Ha på sig is the idiom for wearing clothes. Hon har på sig = she has on, meaning she is wearing.

target: Vi träffas varje söndag för att äta middag ihop.
english: We meet every Sunday to eat dinner together.
tip: Träffas ends in -s to mean meet each other. The -s gives a mutual sense, so vi träffas = we meet up.

english: The presents are opened on Christmas Eve.
tip: Swedish uses på for days and holidays. På julafton = on Christmas Eve, just as på söndag = on Sunday.

english: The flowers are watered every other day.
tip: Varannan means every other. Varannan dag = every other day, alternating between on days and off days.

english: The coffee is brewed at eight o'clock.
tip: Adding -tiden to a clock hour means around that time. Vid åttatiden = around eight, not exactly eight.

english: The beach we used to visit.
tip: Brukade plus an infinitive means used to. Brukade besöka = used to visit, for a past habit that has stopped.

english: The cabin where we used to live.
tip: For a place, use där (where) instead of som. Stugan där vi brukade bo = the cabin where we used to live.
